intro: An ancient {noun}, its surface worn smooth by centuries of unknown hands.
A weathered {noun}, half-buried when it was found, still faintly warm to the touch.
This {noun} hums faintly when held, as though something inside it is still awake.
No two accounts of this {noun} agree on where it came from, only that it was never meant to be found.
The {noun} is heavier than it looks, and colder than the air around it.
Strange markings cover the {noun}, in a script no scholar of this age can read.
Dust never seems to settle on this {noun}, no matter how long it sits untouched.
The {noun} was pried from something's grip. What, exactly, nobody wants to guess.
curse: Those who carried it before you did not carry it for long.
It resents being owned, and it has ways of making that known.
Old wives say something like this chooses its victims, not the other way around.
You can feel it watching you from inside your pack, waiting for the right moment.
It grants strength, yes — but strength borrowed always comes due.
knowledge: Whatever knowledge it holds was never meant to be understood by the living.
Reading it feels like remembering something that never happened to you.
Every page, every rune, seems to cost something to understand.
The wisdom inside is real. So is the price for keeping it.
haunting: {name} did not rest easy, and neither, it seems, does what he left behind.
There is a presence bound to it — patient, cold, and not entirely gone.
Sometimes, in the dark, you swear you hear it breathing.
It was not meant to be carried alone. It no longer is.
lore: {name} killed his brother with this {noun}. His brother's ghost supposedly follows whoever carries it.
It is said {name} never let this {noun} out of his sight, not even in death.
The last owner's name was scratched out of every record that mentions this {noun}.
Legend credits {name} with both its making and its ruin, though no two tellings agree which came first.
{name}'s name is carved into it in letters too small to have been written by human hands.
guardian: It was carried by those sworn to protect something greater than themselves.
Whatever it once guarded is long gone. The habit of guarding, however, remains.
It seems to settle, almost gratefully, into the hands of someone willing to stand and hold a line.
blessing: Rare among things pulled from the dark, this one seems to mean you well.
It carries no weight of malice — only the quiet favor of something long forgotten.
Holding it feels, for once, like being looked after rather than watched.
loss_note: Something about it draws on your own vitality just to remain whole.
You feel a little thinner, a little less yourself, the longer you carry it.
It borrows from your strength to keep its secrets intact.
